title: Feeling the Beat
description: Beats, bars and counting to four, plus the three drums that hold most songs together.

steps.title: The pulse
steps.description: Rhythm is how sounds are laid out in time. Underneath it all is the beat, the steady pulse you tap your foot to. Beats come in groups called bars (or measures), and most pop and rock songs group them in fours.

steps.title: Counting in 4/4
steps.description:
That four-beat feel is written as 4/4:
• Top number: four beats in each bar
• Bottom number: each beat is a quarter note

Count along out loud: 1, 2, 3, 4, 1, 2, 3, 4. Beat 1 is the strongest, and 3 is a little strong too. Beats 2 and 4 are where the snare usually lands in rock and pop.

steps.title: The kick on 1
steps.description: The kick drum usually marks beat 1, the start of every bar. Hit the kick.

steps.title: The snare on 2 and 4
steps.description: A snare hit on beats 2 and 4 is called the backbeat. It's the part people clap along to. Hit the snare.

steps.title: The hi-hat keeps time
steps.description: The closed hi-hat ticks along on every beat, or twice per beat, like a clock holding everything steady. Hit the hi-hat.

steps.title: All three at once
steps.description: In a real groove these three take turns and overlap. For now, hit kick, snare and hi-hat together and hear how they stack into one big sound.
steps.hint: Hit KCK, SNR and CHH at the same moment.

steps.title: Beats in a bar
steps.description: In 4/4 time, how many beats are there in one bar?
